mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the injectivity constraint on forAttempt. The injected violation forces two distinct AuditEntries to share the same AccessAttempt, exactly the 'one entry was mutated/replaced by another' scenario the AppendOnly and FR_010 assertions are designed to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: AuditEntry | e1.forAttempt = e2.forAttempt }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the requirement that every LookupRecord AccessAttempt produces exactly one AuditEntry. The injection forces a LookupRecord attempt with Permitted outcome to have no corresponding AuditEntry — a record was observed without an audit trail, violating SC-001/SC-002.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some a: AccessAttempt | a.kind = LookupRecord and a.outcome = Permitted and (no e: AuditEntry | e.forAttempt = a) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the biconditional that ties Permitted outcomes to active care-team memberships. The injection forces a Permitted AccessAttempt for which no active CareTeamMembership exists — a clinician outside the care team successfully reads a patient record, violating FR-006 and SC-010.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CareTeamGatingViolation { some a: AccessAttempt | a.kind = LookupRecord and a.outcome = Permitted and (no m: CareTeamMembership | m.ctmClinician = a.caller and m.ctmPatient = a.targetPatient and m.ctmStatus = Active) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the constraint that Denied and NotFoundOrDenied must map to NotFoundShape. The injection forces a Denied outcome to carry SuccessShape, distinguishing 'patient exists but you cannot see it' from 'patient not found', leaking patient existence to an unauthorised caller.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoInformationLeakageViolation { some a: AccessAttempt | a.outcome = Denied and a.externalResponse = SuccessShape }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the requirement that an AuditEntry's recordedRole matches the caller's actual role. The injection forces an entry whose recorded role differs from the caller's role — a mis-attribution that would produce a misleading audit trail for IG investigators.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionCorrectnessViolation { some e: AuditEntry | e.recordedRole != e.forAttempt.caller.role }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the permission matrix fact leaves Allowed unconstrained. The injection explicitly adds AuditOfficer -> LookupRecord to the matrix, which violates LeastPrivilege (IG officer gains patient-record access), PrivilegeMonotonicity (roles are no longer disjoint), FR_011 (SearchAudit exclusivity broken), and PermissionCompleteness (#Allowed > 5).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionMatrixViolation { AuditOfficer -> LookupRecord in PermMatrix.Allowed }
